metadata.title: Teacher self-efficacy and self-reported cognitive activation and classroom management: A multilevel perspective on the role of school characteristics

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study re-analysed TALIS 2018 teacher and school questionnaire data for Austria (ISCED level 2), using the teacher and school level weights provided in the TALIS dataset as recommended for multilevel analyses. The authors implemented these complex-sampling weights in Mplus (as per TALIS guidance and multilevel weighting recommendations), rather than treating observations as i.i.d. They used listwise deletion for missing values in the multilevel regression framework. No replicate-weight scheme (e.g., BRR/jackknife) is reported, so uncertainty quantification is described through the multilevel modeling approach with the provided TALIS weights.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This study models teacher self-efficacy and self-reported instructional quality (cognitive activation and classroom management) from TALIS questionnaire responses, not cognitive achievement scores with plausible values. TALIS does not generate PV-based achievement scales in the way PISA/TIMSS do for student test performance, so PV handling is not applicable. Missing data handling is explicitly described as listwise deletion, so the missing-data strategy is not a reporting gap.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Secondary analysis of TALIS 2018 country-level data restricted to Austria, with participation at ISCED level 2. The analytic sample includes teachers who responded to the TALIS teacher questionnaire within the participating schools (246 schools), and the study uses listwise deletion for missing values in the multilevel regression analyses.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Random-intercept model (Table 2): Level 1 self-efficacy in instruction B=0.28 (SE=0.02), β=0.30; Level 2 self-efficacy in instruction B=0.38 (SE=0.09), β=0.66. Context effect (RQ2): school-level efficacy in instruction b(SE)=0.11 (0.09), β=0.25, p=.26; external school characteristics (collaboration b(SE)=-0.00 (0.02), β=-0.03, p=.85; participation b(SE)=-0.00 (0.02), β=-0.01, p=.97; principal leadership b(SE)=-0.02 (0.02), β=-0.07, p=.71).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TALIS 2018 (Austria, ISCED level 2) teacher questionnaire the study leveraged self-efficacy in instruction and school-level efficacy in instruction to predict teacher-reported cognitive activation, finding significant positive associations at both the teacher level (B=0.28) and the school level (B=0.38). This indicates that strengthening teachers’ instructional self-efficacy and fostering efficacious school climates may be associated with higher cognitive activation, although the cross-sectional design and the lack of PV-based achievement outcomes limit causal interpretation.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Random-intercept model (Table 2): Level 1 self-efficacy in classroom management B=0.49 (SE=0.03), β=0.34; Level 2 self-efficacy in classroom management B=0.93 (SE=0.11), β=0.68. Context effect (RQ2): unique school-level efficacy in classroom management b(SE)=0.45 (0.12), β=0.43, p<.001; principal leadership b(SE)=-0.06 (0.03), β=-0.22, p=.03; school-level efficacy in instruction b(SE)=0.15 (0.14), β=0.14, p=.29. Cross-level interactions (Table 3): efficacy in classroom management × school-level efficacy in classroom management B=-0.45 (SE=0.17), p<.05; efficacy in instruction × collaboration B=0.09 (SE=0.05), p<.05.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TALIS 2018 (Austria, ISCED level 2) teacher questionnaire the study leveraged self-efficacy in classroom management, school-level efficacy in classroom management, and principal instructional leadership to predict teacher-reported classroom management, finding significant positive effects for both teacher-level and school-level classroom-management efficacy (Level 1 B=0.49; Level 2 B=0.93) and a strong unique context effect for school-level classroom-management efficacy (b=0.45, p<.001). This indicates that school-level support for effective classroom management—along with leadership practices—may be associated with better classroom management, while moderation effects suggest the relationship between teacher efficacy and classroom management depends on school context.

data.outcome_summary: This study re-analysed TALIS 2018 teacher and principal questionnaire data for Austria (ISCED level 2), focusing on multilevel associations between teacher self-efficacy and two indicators of self-reported instructional quality: cognitive activation and classroom management. Using multilevel random-intercept and random-slope regression models in Mplus (with TALIS-provided teacher and school weights) and listwise deletion for missing values, the authors found significant positive relationships between teacher self-efficacy and both instructional-quality facets at the teacher level and, more strongly, at the school level. For cognitive activation, school-level efficacy in instruction showed significant between-school associations, but unique context effects of school characteristics were not significant. For classroom management, unique school-level efficacy in classroom management was strongly associated with higher classroom management, and principal leadership showed a significant (negative) association. The study is cross-sectional and relies on teacher self-reports, so directionality and causal claims cannot be inferred.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The paper does not train or evaluate machine-learning predictive models; it uses multilevel regression/correlation-style analyses in Mplus/R. Therefore, ML technique fields are intentionally empty (no algorithms to report), and the extraction focuses on multilevel statistical associations rather than ML performance.
